title: Good Tools Are Invisible
summary: A philosophical reflection on tool design philosophy, arguing that the best tools are those that become invisible—meaning they integrate so seamlessly into the workflow that users don't consciously think about them. The article explores how well-designed developer tools should reduce cognitive load rather than add complexity.
problem_solved: Addresses the problem of tools that demand too much attention and cognitive effort from users, making workflows feel cumbersome rather than natural.
why_valuable: Provides a mental model for evaluating and designing tools that truly enhance productivity by disappearing into the background of work.
